newsitem.title: USA: Cold airmass not threatening Brazil coffee - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Cold airmass not threatening Brazil coffee - WSC.

text.p: A storm system is expected to intensify off the south coast of Brazil in the next few days, however the airmass should not be cold enough to cause damage in coffee-growing regions, Weather Services Corp said in an update on Wednesday.

"Computer guidance continues to suggest that this airmass will not be cold enough to cause damage in the coffee belt as it appears to lack a real connection with the polar regions in the far south of Argentina," WSC said.

According to WSC, high pressure is expected to build over central Argentina on Friday and will move into the coffee belt over the weekend. Low temperatures could fall to 39-46 F (4-8 C) on Sunday and Monday mornings.
While no damaging cold is indicated at this time, WSC said the "situation continues to bear close watching."

For the next 48 hours, mostly cloudy skies are predicted with scattered showers and thunderstorms. Partial clearing is expected on Friday. Temperatures should remain near to below normal with lows in the 50's to 60's F (low to middle teens C).
